title: Quantitative & Population Genetics
text:
This course develops the theoretical and statistical foundations of quantitative and population genetics, with emphasis on mathematical formulation and computational implementation.
We study how genetic variation arises, how it is maintained in populations, and how it influences complex traits. The course integrates classical genetic theory with modern statistical modeling approaches used in genomics and prediction.

title: Quantitative & Population Genetics
text:
Core Themes
The material is organized around five central themes:

Genetic Variation

Mendelian inheritance
Allele and genotype frequencies
Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium
Linkage disequilibrium

Quantitative Genetic Models

Linear models in genetics
Variance decomposition
Heritability
Genetic covariance

Mixed Models and Prediction

BLUP
Genomic relationship matrices
Prediction of breeding values

Bayesian Methods

Bayesian linear regression
Shrinkage priors
Marker effect modeling
MCMC principles

Evolutionary Dynamics

Selection response
Drift and mutation
Long-term genetic change

title: Quantitative & Population Genetics
text:
Learning Objectives
After completing the course, students should be able to:

Formulate linear and mixed models for genetic data

Derive expressions for genetic variance components

Interpret heritability in different contexts

Implement genomic prediction models in R

Explain the interaction between selection, drift, and mutation

Connect statistical models with biological interpretation

title: Quantitative & Population Genetics
text:
Structure of the Book
The course is organized sequentially. Each chapter builds on previous material.
Chapters include:

Mathematical derivations

Conceptual explanations

Computational demonstrations in R

Figures and simulation examples

Students are encouraged to work through code examples to develop practical understanding.

title: Quantitative & Population Genetics
text:
Prerequisites
Students are expected to have:

Basic knowledge of genetics

Introductory statistics

Familiarity with R

title: Quantitative & Population Genetics
text:
Recommended Use
The material is designed to be:

Used during lectures

Reviewed after class

Consulted during project work

Revisited during exam preparation

Mathematical notation and modeling steps are emphasized to support conceptual clarity and reproducibility.

title: Genomics, Systems Biology & Bioinformatics
text:
This course provides a conceptual and computational framework for analyzing molecular data across biological scales, from genome to transcriptome to systems-level organization.
The focus is on understanding how genetic and environmental variation influence molecular phenotypes and complex traits through modern high-throughput technologies and statistical modeling.
The course integrates biological interpretation, statistical methodology, and practical implementation in R.

title: Genomics, Systems Biology & Bioinformatics
text:
Core Themes
The material is organized around five interconnected themes:

Molecular Technologies

DNA sequencing technologies

Genotyping platforms

RNA-seq and transcriptomics

Epigenomic and multi-omics profiling

Genomic Association and Mapping

GWAS principles

Population structure and confounding

Fine-mapping

Functional annotation

Multi-Omics Integration

Transcriptome-wide association

eQTL and regulatory variation

Integrative modeling across data layers

Systems-Level Modeling

Gene regulatory networks

Pathway analysis

Network-based interpretation

Causal modeling concepts

Computational and Statistical Methods

High-dimensional regression

Regularization and shrinkage

Machine learning approaches

Reproducible workflows in R

title: Genomics, Systems Biology & Bioinformatics
text:
Learning Objectives
After completing the course, students should be able to:

Explain how sequencing technologies generate molecular data

Evaluate appropriate statistical models for genomic data

Analyze high-dimensional datasets using R

Interpret GWAS and fine-mapping results

Integrate multi-omics datasets conceptually and computationally

Connect molecular variation to complex phenotypes

title: Genomics, Systems Biology & Bioinformatics
text:
Structure of the Book
The course progresses from molecular data generation to systems-level interpretation.
Each chapter includes:

Conceptual background

Statistical framework

Applied examples

Executable R code

Visualizations and case studies

Students are encouraged to actively reproduce analyses and explore parameter choices to deepen understanding.

title: Genomics, Systems Biology & Bioinformatics
text:
Prerequisites
Students are expected to have:

Basic molecular biology knowledge

Introductory statistics

Familiarity with R

Prior exposure to linear models and quantitative genetics is beneficial but not required.

title: Genomics, Systems Biology & Bioinformatics
text:
Recommended Use
This material is designed to support:

Lecture-based instruction

Computational lab sessions

Project-based learning

Independent exploration of genomic datasets

Emphasis is placed on connecting biological mechanisms with statistical modeling in a reproducible framework.
